title: Daily Dialogue: Teach Him to Ask Before He Commands
summary: Between the ages of 4-6, the child begins to develop the Theory of Mind—he understands that others have thoughts and feelings different from his own. This is a golden window to teach him: how to ask? How to listen? How to recount what happened? The lesson cites the principle, 'The best of you is the best to his family,' and the concept of rifq (gentleness) in questioning. The parent who opens dialogue with his child teaches him that asking is more powerful than commanding, and that a kind word is sadaqah (charity). The lesson offers 5 daily questions with which the parent can initiate dialogue before sleep, all tied to qudwah (exemplary conduct).
try_this: This week: Every night before sleep, ask your child 3 questions from this list: (1) What was the most beautiful thing that happened today? (2) When did you feel happiness? (3) When did you feel sadness, and why? (4) What did you do when you wanted to cry? (5) If you could change one thing about today, what would it be?
reflection_prompts: Have you noticed your child beginning to ask you similar questions during the day?
Which question elicited the deepest response from your child?

review_defects.english: the child begins to develop the Theory of Mind
review_defects.why: The Arabic says 'begins with the theory of mind' (i.e., enters the stage of understanding it), not 'begins to develop' which implies the child is constructing the theory itself. The meaning is slightly altered.

review_defects.english: and the concept of rifq (gentleness) in questioning
review_defects.why: The Arabic directly cites 'gentleness in asking' as a principle, without the word 'concept'. Adding 'the concept of' makes it more abstract and less direct than the original.
